messages:
alex: Heads-up: Packaging pipeline just flagged a checksum mismatch after the gzip optimization step for private-installer v1.9.2-delta. Cosign verification fails on the signed submanifest. Need a quick decision: republish full image (longer) or pin previous stable for canary?

maria: I inspected the artifact: gzip removed trailing zero padding bytes from a helper layer, hence the sha256 changed but content difference is tiny. Cosign fails because signatures were computed pre-gzip.

jamal: +1 to pin previous stable for the initial canary so we don't block the delivery window. Start a rebuild/repack job after canary.

alex: Agreed. Plan: 1) Pin canary to `v1.9.1-stable` for the first wave. 2) Maria to repack and re-sign `v1.9.2` off-hours with gzip step skipped or deterministic pipeline. 3) Deploy window stays at 02:00 UTC tonight. If repack finishes early we can consider a second micro-rollout. @maria can you re-sign and push new submanifest? :thumbsup:

maria: On it. I'll disable the gzip strip option locally, rebuild the delta, compute md5+sha256, cosign with key `release-signer-2024` and upload submanifest to S3: `s3://redwood-packages/private/v1.9.2/repacked-submanifest.json`. Will also publish a short release note in the manifest: "repack to preserve deterministic bytes for signing".

jamal: SRE notes: We'll watch error rate and p50/p95 latency on the canary hosts. Rollback criteria: >5% endpoint errors OR sustained p95 increase >200ms for 5 minutes. If triggered we'll run manual rollback to `v1.9.1-stable` and escalate. I'll pre-configure the fallback route.

deploy-bot: [deploy-bot] Canary rollout scheduled by @alex at 2026-03-21T02:00:00Z for channel `private-vpc` using image tag `v1.9.1-stable` on 3 canary instances. To abort run: `/deploy abort 202603210200-7`. Observability: http://internal/releases/202603210200-7

alex: Good. Also add a quick verification step during canary: run the cosign verify command against the submanifest and the actual OCI blob on the node. Example command to paste into runbook:

```
cosign verify-blob --key ksm://projects/release-signer-2024 s3://redwood-packages/private/v1.9.2/repacked-submanifest.json
sha256sum /var/lib/installer/artifacts/private-installer-v1.9.2-delta.tar.gz
```

maria: I'll push the signed manifest before 01:20 UTC and post the signed manifest checksum here. If the cosign verification fails for the canary we abort and keep pinned image. Planning to rotate signing key only if absolutely necessary (won't during this window).

sre-oncall: I'll be watching logs and health checks live. Jamal, I've added a short alert that fires at 3% errors for faster visibility; we can ignore until 5% for automatic rollback threshold but we want eyes earlier.

alex: Sounds good. Final call: pin canary to `v1.9.1-stable` now, start repack job, push signed manifest to S3, deploy-bot will run the scheduled canary. If repack completed and validated before end of canary we can promote in a follow-up patch release.

maria: Uploaded signed submanifest: `s3://redwood-packages/private/v1.9.2/repacked-submanifest.json` SHA256: `b94f6f125f...` (reaction :eyes:). I'll send a short release-note blurb to the release notes doc.

deploy-bot: [deploy-bot] Canary started: id=202603210200-7  — pinned image `v1.9.1-stable`. Monitor at http://internal/releases/202603210200-7/metrics

jamal: Canary in progress. Watching latency and errors. If anything suspicious I'll issue `/deploy abort 202603210200-7` and switch traffic back to the stable pool.

alex: Thanks all. We'll follow up in #eng-releases with the final outcome and a short postmortem if we had to abort.
